instruction.text: Read the text and fill in the gaps.

atoms.text: The diet of the ancient Maya was mostly made up of the vegetables that they grew, such as squash and maize.
They hunted for meat from animals like deer, monkeys, armadillos and turtles. They also caught lobsters and fish from the sea in coastal areas.
Traditional ancient Maya dishes like tortillas and tamales are still made today across North and Central America.
atoms.sound: ssml: Traditional ancient Maya dishes like torteeyas and tamarleyz are still made today across North and Central America.

atoms.a: What vegetables did the Maya eat?
What meat did the Maya eat?

instruction.text: Drag the flour into the bowl to start making traditional Maya tortillas.

text.text: This is a type of flour made by grinding down maize.

instruction.text: Drag the water into the bowl to form a dough.

text.text: Once the dough is ready, it is flattened and cooked on a hot grill. Finally, toppings like beans, vegetables and meat could be added.

atoms.b: Cacao was a sacred food for the Maya. It was believed to be a gift from the ((++gods animals)).
atoms.sound: Kacow was a sacred food for the Maya. It was believed to be a gift from the gods.

atoms.b: Cacao was ground down into a paste and made into a ((++drink cake)). It was flavoured with chilli peppers, honey and cornmeal.
atoms.sound: Kacow was ground down into a paste and made into a drink. It was flavoured with chilli peppers, honey and cornmeal.

atoms.b: The ((++cacao bean)) drink, called xocolatl, was served to rich people at religious ceremonies and weddings.
atoms.sound: The kacow drink, called shockolattle, was served to rich people at religious ceremonies and weddings.
